qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Midwest branch network density and core checking account inertia create modest customer switching costs. However, banking products are largely commoditized and rate-sensitive. Return on capital consistently falls short of the 12% hurdle (median ROIC 9.2%, ROE ~10%, ROA ~0.95%). The bank possesses zero independent pricing power over loan yields or deposit funding costs across interest rate cycles.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC 9.2% < 12%, lack of pricing power, REJECT). Regional commercial bank operating as a price-taker on both lending spreads and deposit betas. Midwest branch density and Fair Play banking provide customer inertia but fail to generate sustainable returns above the 12% hurdle across economic cycles.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 9.2% fails the 12% capital efficiency threshold. Multi-cycle ROE has averaged 9.5-10.5% with ROA below 1.0% (0.92-0.98% in FY2023-2025). Commercial and consumer loans face aggressive spread competition against money-center peers and private credit. Deposit beta pressures and wholesale funding requirements prevent pricing ahead of inflation. Inherent ~10-12x balance sheet leverage and asset-liability duration mismatch present structural risks typical of fractional-reserve banking.
